children: A power struggle between the Indian group’s holding company and its owners has $260 bln of Tata stock on a rollercoaster ride. But the moves underestimate how the turmoil can hurt operating companies and give pause to business partners from Singapore Airlines to Starbucks.
Full view will be published shortly.
Follow Ujjaini Dutta on LinkedIn and X.

Shares of Tata group companies fell on September 18, with Tata Chemicals down 9.7% in intraday trading, Tata Motors 3.3% and Tata Consultancy 3%. The declines reversed some gains made the previous day.

Shares moved ⁠after Tata Sons, the group's holding company, said it had reappointed N. Chandrasekaran as executive chairman for another five years and would initiate steps to comply with a regulatory order to list itself.

Tata Sons is the privately held holding company for India's Tata conglomerate. The development reverses Chandrasekaran's decision on August 12 to not seek reappointment citing the absence of the board's unanimous support.

Tata Sons' ​65% shareholders, Tata Trusts, dismissed the appointment as "illegal". The Trusts, ​which oppose a listing said Tata Sons' articles of association require both of the Trusts' nominee directors to the Tata Sons board to vote in favour of the chair. Noel Tata, one of the nominees ​and chair of Tata Trusts, voted against the proposal and that makes the reappointment void, the statement added.
On Friday, Shapoorji Pallonji Group, a minority shareholder of Tata Sons, expressed support for a potential listing.
